empty-start.name: Start a local audit
empty-start.goal: Understand what Press does and begin with either a folder or one image without wondering whether files will be uploaded.
success: The primary starting action is obvious.
The local-only privacy promise is clear before choosing a file.
Keyboard and pointer users can reach both supported starting paths.
interaction_trace: Launch Press with no path.
Choose Open folder, Open image, or drop a supported path.

empty-folder.name: Recover from an empty folder
empty-folder.goal: Understand why the chosen folder produced no audit and continue with another folder or one image.
success: The state is clearly different from first launch and scan failure.
The reason and next actions are visible without opening documentation.
Folder, image, and drop recovery paths remain available.
interaction_trace: Open a folder containing no supported images.
Read the reason.
Choose another folder, one image, or drop a supported path.

audit-core.name: Find and prepare costly images
audit-core.goal: Identify which images deserve optimization, understand the conversion target, and commit the correct visible or selected scope.
success: The worst optimization candidates are recognizable without reading documentation.
Filter and selection scope cannot contradict the Convert action.
Output presets, fine tuning, projected result, and commitment read as one decision.
The primary image list remains usable at the minimum supported width.
interaction_trace: Open a folder and inspect the default ordering.
Identify an expensive image and optionally filter or select it.
Choose an output preset or fine-tune format, quality, and maximum size.
Read the estimate and convert the visible or selected target.
review_focus: Relationship between findings, list, output settings, estimate, and commit action
Hierarchy and density across window sizes

keyboard-selection.name: Select an audit row by keyboard
keyboard-selection.goal: Move through the audit, select one image, and understand that conversion now targets the selection.
success: The focused row and selected row are distinguishable.
The output panel immediately names the selected scope.
The conversion command promises the same scope.
interaction_trace: Open a folder.
Press Down to move the cursor.
Press Space to select the row.
Read the updated output scope.

gallery-core.name: Scan audit candidates in the gallery
gallery-core.goal: Recognize image candidates visually, compare their optimization cost, and retain the same selection and conversion model as the list.
success: Images remain scannable without hiding filenames, dimensions, size, or findings.
The gallery and output panel read as one workflow.
Selection, focus, and conversion scope stay predictable across widths.
interaction_trace: Open a folder in gallery view.
Scan thumbnails and file facts for costly candidates.
Select candidates or open one for comparison.
Read and commit the matching output scope.

filter-no-results.name: Recover from a filter with no matches
filter-no-results.goal: Understand that the folder is intact, clear the active filter, and return to the audit without accidentally converting hidden files.
success: The empty list is attributed to the active filter.
Clearing the filter is obvious and keyboard-accessible.
The output scope does not imply that hidden folder contents will be converted.
interaction_trace: Open a folder.
Type a filename filter that matches nothing.
Read the empty result and conversion scope.
Clear the filter to restore the audit.
review_focus: Cause and recovery for zero results

filter-clear-keyboard.name: Clear a filter by keyboard
filter-clear-keyboard.goal: Reach the named filter recovery action by keyboard, activate it, and return to the unchanged audit.
success: Tab moves from the populated filter to its Clear action.
Enter activates Clear and restores every matching row.
Output settings remain unchanged and conversion returns to the full visible scope.
interaction_trace: Focus the filename filter and type a query with no matches.
Press Tab to focus Clear.
Press Enter to clear the query.
Verify the audit and full conversion scope return.

sirv-settings.name: Configure Sirv credentials
sirv-settings.goal: Understand which credentials are required, where they remain, how to save them, and how to leave safely.
success: The form names the account context and both required fields.
The local-storage promise and secret-field behavior are clear.
Save, close, Tab, Shift-Tab, and Escape have predictable ownership.
interaction_trace: Open Settings from the audit or press Control-comma.
Enter a Client ID and Client secret.
Save credentials or close without saving.

sirv-settings-complete.name: Complete the Sirv credential form
sirv-settings-complete.goal: Enter both required credentials by keyboard and make Save available without submitting test values.
success: Typing begins in Client ID after the panel opens.
Tab moves to Client secret and both values remain visible or safely masked.
Save credentials becomes enabled only after both fields contain values.
interaction_trace: Open Settings by keyboard.
Type a Client ID.
Press Tab and type a Client secret.
Verify Save credentials becomes available without activating it.

sirv-settings-save-keyboard.name: Save Sirv credentials by keyboard
sirv-settings-save-keyboard.goal: Complete the credential form and submit it without leaving the keyboard.
success: Enter submits a complete form from the Client secret field.
A visible Saved confirmation appears without exposing the secret.
Focus and the safe Escape route remain predictable after saving.
interaction_trace: Open Settings and type both credentials.
Press Enter from Client secret.
Verify the in-place save result without revealing the secret.

sirv-missing-credentials.name: Recover from missing Sirv credentials
sirv-missing-credentials.goal: Understand why Sirv browsing cannot start and reach the credential setup without editing files by hand.
success: The failure clearly names missing credentials rather than a remote outage.
A visible action leads to the in-app credential form.
Closing or pressing Escape returns to the unchanged local audit.
interaction_trace: Open Sync with Sirv without saved credentials.
Read the cause.
Open credential settings or close and return to the audit.
review_focus: Safe return to the local workflow

sirv-setup-from-error.name: Open Sirv setup from its error
sirv-setup-from-error.goal: Move from the missing-credentials explanation into the in-app credential form without leaving the workflow.
success: The setup action opens the existing Sirv account form.
Initial focus lands in Client ID and Save remains disabled while fields are empty.
The form keeps its purpose, required-field, privacy, and secret-masking guidance.
interaction_trace: Open Sync with Sirv without saved credentials.
Activate Set up Sirv.
Verify the credential form opens ready for input.

conversion-result.name: Understand a completed conversion
conversion-result.goal: Confirm what completed, judge the actual size result, locate the output, and know whether another conversion would replace it.
success: Completion is distinguishable from an estimate and names files, before/after bytes, and savings or growth.
The output-folder action is easy to find.
The original folder remains clearly untouched and the next conversion action is unambiguous.
interaction_trace: Open a folder and accept the current output settings.
Convert all visible files.
Read the completed result and inspect per-file outcomes.
Show the output folder or adjust settings and convert again.

conversion-retune.name: Retune after a completed conversion
conversion-retune.goal: Change quality after conversion and understand that the next run replaces the matching generated outputs with the new setting.
success: Changing quality returns the summary to an estimate without forgetting that outputs exist.
The primary action still predicts replacement and names the affected output count and format.
The output-folder action stays available while considering the new estimate.
interaction_trace: Convert all visible files.
Change the quality after completion.
Read the new estimate and the repeat-conversion action.
review_focus: Repeat action truthfulness after settings change

comparison-core.name: Judge one conversion preview
comparison-core.goal: Compare real original and encoded pixels, understand the size tradeoff, navigate adjacent images, and return to the audit.
success: Original and output sides are identifiable without covering important pixels.
Fit, 100 percent, divider, pan, and navigation controls are discoverable but secondary.
The current output format and size result remain clear.
Failure and loading states cannot be confused with a finished preview.
interaction_trace: Open an image or press Enter on an audit row.
Inspect the fitted split view and drag the divider.
Use 100 percent or zoom and pan when needed.
Move to the previous or next image, then close the comparison.

comparison-tools.name: Choose an auxiliary image tool
comparison-tools.goal: Find background removal, local upscaling, or Sirv Studio without confusing those actions with conversion.
success: Convert remains the only primary action in the comparison header.
One clearly named Tools action reveals all auxiliary image actions.
The disclosed actions remain readable and unclipped at every supported width.
interaction_trace: Open an image comparison.
Activate Tools.
Choose a local image action or Sirv Studio, or dismiss the disclosure.

conversion-running.name: Watch a conversion run
conversion-running.goal: Know that work is under way, how far along it is, what it is producing, and that nothing can be changed until it finishes.
success: Progress is legible without hunting: how many files are done, out of how many.
Every control that would change the outcome mid-run is visibly unavailable.
The action bar and the rail agree about what is happening.
interaction_trace: Open a folder and pick the AVIF preset, which is slow enough to watch.
Start the conversion.
Read progress while it runs and try to change a setting.
review_focus: Which controls lock during a run and how that reads
Agreement between the bar and the rail

local-ai-upscale.name: Upscale one image locally
local-ai-upscale.goal: Tick one image, open the upscale rail, and understand what it will produce, where it lands, and what the first run costs before committing.
success: The two local models are unavailable until exactly one image is ticked, and say why.
The rail names the file, the resulting dimensions, and the model download.
Nothing suggests the image leaves the computer.
interaction_trace: Open a folder and tick one image.
Choose Upscale 4x in the action bar.
Read what the rail promises and commit or close it.
review_focus: Single-image rule and how unavailability reads
What the rail owes you before a 49 MB download
